# packages/collections

The creator content types. Depends on `@creatorkit/tokens`, `@creatorkit/core` and
`@creatorkit/ui`. Nothing depends on this except apps, templates and the Ghost theme.

**Read `INVENTORY.md` before grepping.** 77 classes, generated by `pnpm build`.

## The shape

Every type is `.c` plus a modifier: `.c.c-video`, `.c.c-course`. Shared behaviour lives on
`.c`; the modifier carries only what makes that type different. A new type that needs to
restate padding, radius or hover is a sign the change belongs on `.c` instead.

Decks are the grids: `.deck-c`, `.deck-c-sm`, `.deck-c-lg`, `.deck-c-list`.

## Rules

1. **No new base styles here.** If a type needs a card behaviour that others would want,
   it belongs in `@creatorkit/ui`'s card, not in a `.c-*` modifier.
2. **A type is a noun a creator uses**, not a layout. `c-video` and `c-trip` are types;
   "wide card" is not — that is a deck variant.
3. **The page templates beside each stylesheet are documentation.** `travel/index.html`
   shows how a trip is meant to be laid out. Keep them working when the CSS changes.
4. No hardcoded design values. Everything resolves against the foundation's tokens.

## Adding a type

Add the modifier to `styles/collection.css` if it only needs the shared card, or a folder
with its own stylesheet if it needs more. Add it to `collectionTypes` in `src/index.ts` so
the union stays honest, add the `@import` to `styles/index.css` if you made a folder, then
`pnpm build`.

## Testing

`pnpm --filter @creatorkit/collections build`, then look at the type's page on the docs
site under **The kit → Collections**. There is no unit test for a stylesheet worth
writing; the demo pages are the test.
